paper.title: Language Generation in the Limit
paper.summary: Introduces generation in the limit from exact positive presentations and proves countable-family generation, a stronger uniform guarantee for finite families, and prompted extensions.

formalization_scope.summary: The central countable-family result has semantic, observed-set, and NeurIPS finite-query paths over Nat, and the finite-query theorem is transported to every explicitly enumerable countably infinite universe. The finite-family result has a native fixed-sample membership-query scan with an infinite pairwise-distinct output sequence and the same universe transports. Robust-prompt Theorem 7.1 remains unformalized.
specializations: Lean uses zero-based language and universe indices.
gaps: P01 robust-prompt Theorem 7.1 is not formalized.

The informal pairwise-distinct-output modification of the countable-family Theorem 2.1 constructions is not formalized; Theorem 2.2's separate pairwise-distinct conclusion is complete, and P39 proves non-repetition for a materially different patient machine.

claims.title: Countable-family generation in the limit
claims.statement_summary: For every countably indexed family of infinite languages with uniform membership access, one target-independent algorithm eventually outputs a fresh element of the hidden target after every exact positive presentation of that target.

source_assessment.notes: The active formalization follows the NeurIPS proceedings endpoint-test algorithm.

formalization.notes: The three original paths prove the Nat result. The explicit-equivalence transport theorem preserves the finite-membership-query interface over an arbitrary universe, and a classical convenience wrapper supplies the coding from Countable plus the family's infinitude.

components.summary: Countable-family generation in the limit over Nat, with the NeurIPS finite-query machine and two semantic interfaces.
Transport the concrete finite-query Nat construction to every explicitly enumerable countable universe in the source theorem.

lean_links.notes: Implements the proceedings endpoint-search algorithm without receiving the target index or a convergence threshold.
Mirrors the round-dependent Section 4 construction with time supplied explicitly; it is not the finite-query implementation of Theorem 2.1.
Supplies the literal observed-set semantic route, using distinct-observation cardinality as the candidate scope.
Encodes the family, presentation, and membership queries along an explicit equivalence, runs the NeurIPS machine over Nat, and decodes its output while preserving target membership and freshness.
Convenience wrapper that classically selects an equivalence with Nat. It proves the abstract countable-universe proposition but does not claim that the selected coding is executable.

relations.notes: Both establish the same eventual validity/freshness criterion through different interfaces; the finite-query machines do not depend on the SetInterface construction.

claims.title: Uniform finite-family generation
claims.statement_summary: For every finite family there is a family-dependent sample bound after which one algorithm can produce an infinite pairwise-distinct sequence of fresh target elements, uniformly over the target and the sufficiently large finite sample.

source_assessment.notes: The NeurIPS theorem has the stated family-uniform threshold and pairwise-distinct output-sequence guarantee.

formalization.notes: The native P01 construction reuses the existing uniform Boolean membership oracle, filters a supplied finite index set against one fixed sample, and successively searches for common accepted points outside that sample. A Core finite-class closure bound gives one family-dependent threshold; strict growth of the search outputs gives the paper's infinite pairwise-distinct sequence. Explicit-equivalence and classical countable-universe transports are also proved.

components.summary: One generator and one family-dependent distinct-sample threshold give persistent fresh target outputs uniformly over every target in a finite class.
A P01-style membership-query procedure generates from an arbitrary fixed sufficiently large finite target sample.
The procedure returns an infinite sequence of pairwise-distinct elements of the target outside the fixed sample.

lean_links.notes: Represents the finite collection by a Finset of indices in the existing OracleFamily. The family-uniform threshold is selected from its finite closure dimension; the output scan is target-independent by proof irrelevance. No numerical query or runtime bound is claimed.
Encodes the sample and oracle family along the supplied equivalence, runs the Nat scan, and decodes the injective output sequence.
Convenience wrapper that classically selects the universe coding; the explicit-equivalence theorem is the algorithmic interface.

A cross-paper P02 theorem independently packages the related online uniform fresh-output consequence through the same Core finite-class closure fact. It is supporting comparison evidence, not the P01 fixed-sample algorithm.

relations.notes: This is the finite-family theorem with a stronger family-uniform threshold and output-sequence guarantee.

claims.title: Finite-set semantic generation function
claims.statement_summary: Every countable family admits a semantic function of the observed finite set alone that is eventually fresh and correct along every exact presentation of a target language.

source_assessment.notes: The literal claim is retained, but the published round-dependent construction (4.5) is not itself a function of the observed set when repetitions occur. Lean supplies a cardinality-scope repair.

formalization.notes: The repetition-tolerant theorem proves the literal observed-set conclusion over Nat and repairs the paper's round-versus-set construction mismatch. No generic transport theorem covers the source's arbitrary explicitly enumerable countable universe.

components.summary: A repetition-tolerant finite-set-only semantic generation function over Nat.
Transport the finite-set-only construction to every explicitly enumerable countable universe in the source claim.

lean_links.notes: Uses the number of distinct observations rather than elapsed time as the candidate scope.
Adds injectivity so the observed-set cardinality equals the elapsed round.
Receives the elapsed round separately and therefore mirrors (4.5) without realizing the literal finite-set-only interface.

relations.notes: Both establish the same eventual validity/freshness criterion through different interfaces; the finite-query machines do not depend on the SetInterface construction.

claims.title: Robust-prompt generation
claims.statement_summary: Given an exact target presentation and prompts robust for every candidate language, a membership-query algorithm eventually returns a fresh target string extending each current prompt.

source_assessment.notes: The active source inventory follows the NeurIPS statement and its Appendix A.5 proof.

formalization.notes: The library has no P01 string/concatenation/prefix prompt model, robustness predicate, or matching prompted generator. P02's multiclass prompted interface is materially different.

relations.notes: Adds a prompt-extension requirement to fresh target generation.

audit_refs.scope: Historical source inventory and omission analysis; the active claim uses the NeurIPS Theorem 7.1 statement.

claims.title: Pairwise-distinct generated-output strengthening
claims.statement_summary: The countable-family semantic and finite-query constructions for Theorem 2.1 can reportedly be modified so that generated outputs are pairwise distinct, not merely fresh relative to the adversary's observed sample.

source_assessment.notes: The strengthening is stated informally rather than as a numbered theorem.

formalization.notes: The registered Theorem 2.1 constructions require freshness only relative to the adversary sample and have not been extended with output history. Theorem 2.2's separate fixed-sample output sequence is now pairwise distinct, but it is not this modification of the countable-family machines. P39 proves non-repetition for a materially different patient machine.

lean_links.notes: A different patient-scope machine proves eventual target validity, sample freshness, output non-repetition, and a lower-density bound.
Proves injectivity of the P39 output stream independently of the P01 algorithms.

relations.notes: Strengthens the output specification; no strict separation is claimed.
